h: Making Lakeside more than a shopping trip
p: Escape rooms are brilliant at turning an ordinary day into something people actually talk about. If you've got a family who groan at the thought of another shopping trip, booking a game is a sneaky way to get them on board. Teenagers, especially, tend to perk up when there's a mystery to crack and a timer to beat.

A few pointers for your game. Before you start, agree on simple roles: someone to keep an eye on the clock, someone to look after the items you've found, and someone to ask for a hint when the group's really stuck. Search the whole room before trying to solve anything, and say out loud what you've spotted. Small details, like a pattern or a number, often turn out to be the key to the next step.

Beyond the shops and the lakeside boardwalk with its restaurants, Thurrock has some surprising outings close by. Grays Beach Riverside Park, down by the Thames, has a big play area and river views, making it a handy spot for families to run about. History buffs can head to Tilbury Fort, the impressive star-shaped fortress run by English Heritage on the riverbank, or Coalhouse Fort at East Tilbury, another Victorian defence on the Thames. If you're making a weekend of it, the North Kent coast and the Essex countryside are both within easy reach thanks to the area's road links. Do keep an eye on traffic around the Dartford Crossing, as it can get very busy at peak times, and give yourselves a buffer before your booked slot so a jam on the M25 doesn't eat into your game.
